definition.def: When you come to a conclusion, you decide that something is true after you have thought about it carefully and have considered all the relevant facts.
examples: Over the years I've come to the conclusion that she's a very great musician.
I know I'm doing the right thing but other people will draw their own conclusions.

definition.def: The conclusion of something is its ending.
examples: At the conclusion of the programme, I asked the children if they had any questions. [+ of]

definition.def: The conclusion of a treaty or a business deal is the act of arranging it or agreeing it.
examples: ...the expected conclusion of a free-trade agreement between the two countries. [+ of]

definition.def: You can refer to something that seems certain to happen as a foregone conclusion.
examples: It was a foregone conclusion that I would end up in the same business as him.
The championship result was almost a foregone conclusion.

definition.def: You say 'in conclusion' to indicate that what you are about to say is the last thing that you want to say.
examples: In conclusion, walking is a cheap, safe, enjoyable and readily available form of exercise.

definition.def: If you say that someone jumps to a conclusion, you are critical of them because they decide too quickly that something is true, when they do not know all the facts. [disapproval]
examples: I didn't want her to jump to the conclusion that the divorce was in any way her fault. [PHRASE that]
Forgive me. I shouldn't be jumping to conclusions.
